sonnet.problem: Verse 18 says only that 'they brought us' the Levites. It never says Ezra's team went to Casiphia and 'came back' with them, or who 'they' are. The card states a link the text leaves open. Card 10 repeats it ('Ezra's team also brings 220 ... servants').
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open. Who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The wrong answers 'palace' and 'royal' mean nearly the same thing as each other (palace servants and royal servants).
sonnet.rule: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it. Two wrong answers never mean the same as each other either.

sonnet.problem: Hashabiah first appears here with no introduction. Stop 1 never mentioned him, and his Levite identity from the descendants of Merari (8:19) goes untold.
sonnet.rule: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

sonnet.problem: The question says the priests guard the treasure 'until they reach the house of the LORD in Jerusalem.' Card 10 then asks where they weigh it out, and its right answer is 'In the house of God.' The earlier question gives that answer away.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: Cards 3, 7, 11 and 13 all use the same punchline shape: Papa Dorin fumbles something small in his bakery (oven timer, one cookie box, watching an oven, two dozen cookies) next to the huge thing in the passage. That is one joke shape used four times in a single lesson.
sonnet.rule: Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson.
